about: The shot catalog shared by the script writer (module 7) and the video step (module 8), settled Nov 26 (Jan: all as recommended). The writer picks one shot per beat and fills only that shot's blanks; every other blank stays empty ("" or []). Word marks in the narration look like [count 1,250 homes]: the mark's name, then the spoken words an animation follows. The writer aims at words_min to words_max and at most hook_words_max; a script is refused only below words_hard_min, above words_hard_max or with a hook above hook_words_hard_max (Jan, Nov 26: slightly over is fine; 115 words is fine when a story has little to say).

tones.serious: calm and plain, like a public broadcaster; short sentences, no exclamation marks
tones.casual: friendly and conversational, like explaining it to a friend; contractions are fine; still no jokes about harm
tones.high-energy: brisk and punchy, short sentences and strong verbs that stay neutral; never hype, never exclamation marks about harm

hook.use: always the first beat: the most important checked fact, or the clash when that fact is disputed

blanks.title: the on-screen headline, at most 7 words, every name and number from the cited claims

blanks.places: exactly 1 place name, as the claims or the event's location name write it
blanks.label: a short on-screen label (optional)

map_link.use: from A to B: a strike path, a bridge, a route, two countries

blanks.places: exactly 2 place names: from, then to
blanks.label: a short on-screen label (optional)
blanks.prop: a prop that travels the arc (optional)

blanks.label: the count label, for example "6 cities"

blanks.card: the Q label of a quote from the quote list
blanks.speaker: the person's name

claim_vs_claim.use: two accounts that disagree, each with who says it

blanks.accounts: exactly 2: who, what they say in at most 6 words, the claim id

blanks.value: the number as the claim writes it
blanks.label: who says it or what it means, a few words

blanks.rows: 2 to 6 rows of label and value

document.use: a ruling, law, sanction or order

blanks.doc_kind: ruling, law, sanction, order, report or other
blanks.title: the document's name

sides.use: how each side tells it: second to last, only in two-sided stories

blanks.points: the side point ids, one or two per side

sources.use: always the last beat: code draws the card (balance bar, outlets, credits, AI mark)

headline.use: a plain line, or the fallback when no other shot fits

blanks.title: the card's text, at most 10 words, every name and number from the cited claims

broll.portrait: a public figure's name, written as in the claims; the video step skips it when it has no portrait
broll.rule: B-roll shows the place, the people and the kind of thing, never the event itself. No victims or injuries.
